questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Describe the transformations mapping y=|x| to y=|x−3|+2. Give the vertex and state whether the resulting graph crosses the x-axis. [4 marks]
markPoints: The term |x−3| shifts the graph of y=|x| three units right.
The +2 shifts the graph two units upwards.
Since |x−3|≥0, y≥2 so there are no x-axis intersections.
questions.modelAnswer: The term |x−3| shifts the graph of y=|x| three units right. The +2 shifts the graph two units upwards. The vertex is (3,2). Since |x−3|≥0, y≥2 so there are no x-axis intersections.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with two equal strips to estimate ∫₀²√(1+x) dx. Give the exact integral and decide if the approximation is an overestimate or underestimate. [5 marks]
markPoints: Since the trapezium value is smaller, it is an underestimate; the graph is concave down.
questions.modelAnswer: The strip width is h=(2−0)/2=1. The three ordinates are 1, √2 and √3. Trapezium estimate=(1/2)(1+2√2+√3)≈2.78024. The exact integral is [(2/3)(1+x)^(3/2)]₀²=(2/3)(3√3−1)≈2.79743. Since the trapezium value is smaller, it is an underestimate; the graph is concave down.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: The smooth curve y=(x−2)²+3 passes through (2,3). Find the tangent and normal lines at (2,3), explaining their gradients. [3 marks]
markPoints: dy/dx=2(x−2), so at x=2 the gradient is zero.
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent and vertical: x=2.
questions.modelAnswer: dy/dx=2(x−2), so at x=2 the gradient is zero. The tangent is horizontal: y=3. The normal is perpendicular to the tangent and vertical: x=2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For x>0, express (6−x^(3/2))/x² in the form 6x^p−x^q. Find p, q and explain the domain. [4 marks]
markPoints: Also x^(3/2)/x²=x^(−1/2), so q=−1/2; the given real expression has x>0.
questions.modelAnswer: Split the fraction into 6/x²−x^(3/2)/x². Use x^a/x^b=x^(a−b). Therefore 6/x²=6x^(−2), so p=−2. Also x^(3/2)/x²=x^(−1/2), so q=−1/2; the given real expression has x>0.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For y=5e^(3x), find x at the point where y=35 and then obtain the gradient there. [4 marks]
markPoints: Differentiate using the chain rule: dy/dx=15e^(3x).
At y=35, e^(3x)=7, so the gradient is 15×7=105.
questions.modelAnswer: Set 5e^(3x)=35, so e^(3x)=7. Take logs: x=(ln7)/3. Differentiate using the chain rule: dy/dx=15e^(3x). At y=35, e^(3x)=7, so the gradient is 15×7=105.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x²(x+4) and p(x)=f(x)+25. Give the intercepts and crossing/touching behaviour of f, show that x+5 is a factor of p, factorise p fully over real factors, and state the transformation from f to p. [6 marks]
markPoints: The real roots of f are x=−4 and x=0.
The simple root at −4 crosses the axis, while the repeated root at zero touches it.
The quadratic discriminant is (−1)²−4(1)(5)=−19<0, so p has only the one real root, −5.
The graph is translated 25 units upwards.
questions.modelAnswer: The real roots of f are x=−4 and x=0. The simple root at −4 crosses the axis, while the repeated root at zero touches it. p(−5)=25(−5+4)+25=0, so x+5 is a factor. Polynomial division gives p(x)=(x+5)(x²−x+5). The quadratic discriminant is (−1)²−4(1)(5)=−19<0, so p has only the one real root, −5. The graph is translated 25 units upwards.
questions.manualReviewReason: Compare the student's reasoning with each step, accepting algebraically equivalent valid working.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: A circular sector has fixed perimeter 20 cm, radius r and angle θ radians, with 0<θ≤2π. Find the θ that maximises its area and determine the maximum area. [6 marks]
markPoints: For 0<θ<2 this derivative is positive and for 2<θ≤2π it is negative, so θ=2 radians gives the maximum.
The maximum area is A(2)=200×2/4²=25 cm².
questions.modelAnswer: Perimeter 20=2r+rθ=r(θ+2). Hence r=20/(θ+2). The sector area A=(1/2)r²θ=200θ/(θ+2)². Differentiate to obtain dA/dθ=200(2−θ)/(θ+2)³. For 0<θ<2 this derivative is positive and for 2<θ≤2π it is negative, so θ=2 radians gives the maximum. The maximum area is A(2)=200×2/4²=25 cm².

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Evaluate exactly ∫₀¹ x³/√(x⁴+1) dx using substitution, including the changed limits. [5 marks]
markPoints: The new limits are u=1 when x=0 and u=2 when x=1.
questions.modelAnswer: Put u=x⁴+1, so du=4x³dx. The new limits are u=1 when x=0 and u=2 when x=1. The integral becomes (1/4)∫₁² u^(−1/2) du. Integrate to give (1/2)[√u]₁². Therefore the exact result is (√2−1)/2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 3 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For t≥0 a curve is given parametrically by x=t+t², y=t². Obtain dy/dx in terms of t and find its tangent at t=1. [4 marks]
markPoints: At t=1 the coordinates are (2,1) and the gradient is 2/3.
questions.modelAnswer: dx/dt=1+2t and dy/dt=2t. Therefore dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt)=2t/(1+2t). At t=1 the coordinates are (2,1) and the gradient is 2/3. The tangent is y−1=(2/3)(x−2).
